rule_summary: Xcel offers an optional Value of Solar (VOS) tariff as an alternative to standard NEM for residential/small customers, and VOS became mandatory (not optional) for new Community Solar Garden subscribers under a phased ARR-to-VOS transition effective April 1 2025 (Docket E002/M-21-694). Xcel also runs Solar*Rewards, a 10-year performance-based incentive (~$0.03/kWh in 2026) paid on all production regardless of export, stackable with standard NEM bill credits. Standard NEM credits banked in a 'Solar Bank' with annual true-up in April.
export_credit_value: Standard NEM average retail credit ~$0.11-0.13/kWh (2025-2026); VOS for CSG subscribers ~$0.1909/kWh (2025 filing); Solar*Rewards PBI adder $0.03/kWh (2026 vintage)
non_export_option: Yes — Xcel MN Electric Energy Storage Interconnection Guidelines define a formal non-export operating mode using customer-provided control-system settings verified via bi-directional metering to confirm zero export compliance
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited for non-export configurations (energy used to charge from grid is not compensated and does not earn Solar*Rewards/VOS credit; exported energy from a grid-charged battery is generally not eligible for NEM credit under standard interconnection agreement — confirm case-by-case with utility DER team)

standby_charge: Net metering grid access charge (utility-specific fee, amount not published in sources reviewed) applied to solar/DG accounts in addition to basic service and energy charges

rule_summary: NEM threshold (CGS Net Metered rate) is <300 kW aggregate nameplate, well above the 20 kW PSC 119 statewide default. Excess above monthly consumption is NOT credited at retail — paid at a separate 'Avoided Energy Cost Rate' tied to day-ahead LMP for the WEC.S MISO pricing zone, updated annually Jan 1 (flat rate $0.03177/kWh in 2025; TOU on/off-peak variants). Avoided Capacity Cost Rate and Avoided Transmission Cost Rate both currently $0.00000/kWh — i.e. no capacity/transmission value paid to DG customers as of 2025 tariff. Generation Customer Charge applied per meter per day ($0.05951 residential/non-demand secondary; $0.15255 demand secondary; $3.14334 primary) in addition to standard customer charge. Telemetry Charge ($0.73071/day) required for systems >=300 kW where excess energy anticipated (utility does not use telemetry to control customer generation).
export_credit_value: Avoided Energy Cost Rate: $0.03177/kWh flat (2025); TOU: summer on-peak $0.04064 / off-peak $0.02852; non-summer on-peak $0.03411 / off-peak $0.02931 (updated annually Jan 1 based on WEC.S zone day-ahead LMP forecast)
non_export_option: Non-Purchase (CGS NP) option allows generation up to 15 MW with zero compensation for any inadvertent export (a de facto non-export/self-consumption path); Direct Sale-Fixed Price and Customer Use rate options exist for QF-certified generators up to 5 MW
standby_charge: Generation Customer Charge: $0.05951/day (residential/non-demand secondary), $0.15255/day (demand secondary), $3.14334/day (primary) — in addition to standard customer charge; separate Telemetry Charge $0.73071/day for systems >=300 kW with anticipated export

rule_summary: Net Metering (Pg-2) applies to systems <=100 kW (state default is 20 kW — MGE is well above); Parallel Generation (Pg-1) rate applies above 100 kW. For net metering customers, exported energy credited at same retail rate as imported energy (1:1) for the first 12 months. Beginning month 13, if the customer has been a net exporter over the trailing 12 months ('Net Seller'), excess credits roll over at the lower Parallel Generation Buyback Rate instead of retail rate — a significant behind-the-scenes de-rate for oversized systems not paired with storage. MGE guidance explicitly warns customers not to oversize solar without adding a battery, given this Net Seller de-rate.
export_credit_value: Year 1: retail rate (1:1); Year 13+ for Net Sellers: Parallel Generation Buyback Rate (lower than retail, exact cents/kWh not confirmed in sources reviewed)

rule_summary: Alliant purchases excess solar generation at the retail rate up to the customer's monthly usage; production beyond monthly usage is credited at an 'Avoided Cost' rate (~$0.03-0.07/kWh range, fluctuates). export_credit_value: Within-month usage: retail rate; excess beyond monthly usage: Avoided Cost, approx. $0.03-0.07/kWh (fluctuates, exact current figure not confirmed in sources reviewed)

utility_name: Northern States Power Co - Wisconsin (Xcel Energy)
rule_summary: NEM threshold is <=100 kW (state default is 20 kW — Xcel-WI is above default, matching Xcel-MN's 40kW-adjacent generosity). Excess exported energy credited at full retail rate with monthly banking/rollover (unlike immediate avoided-cost payout used by some other WI utilities). Any credits remaining as of January 1 are paid out via check, valued using a weighted average of on-peak/off-peak seasonal wholesale prices per the Pg-2B tariff — notably higher effective compensation than We Energies or WPL's avoided-cost-based approaches, described by IREC as the strongest NEM policy among major Wisconsin utilities.

rule_summary: SMECO is a cooperative but, unlike Delaware's DEC, MD's COMAR 20.50 net metering/interconnection rules are written to bind 'electric companies' inclusive of cooperatives -- SMECO's PSC Net Metering Report data (avg. April 2025 credit $58.08 across 3,612 residential accounts) is reported alongside the IOUs under the same statewide cap/sizing framework, with no distinct SMECO-specific cap or sizing deviation identified. NOT independently confirmed among the four utilities that filed 2020 PSC storage pilot proposals (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison) -- SMECO does not appear to have participated in the utility-owned storage pilot program, which may mean SMECO territory has less utility-side storage infrastructure/experience than the four Exelon/FirstEnergy utilities, though this is an inference, not a confirmed absence.
storage_specific_notes: No SMECO-specific storage tariff or BYOD program identified in sources reviewed this pass -- if SMECO customers want compensated storage participation, the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilots (BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison) do NOT appear to include SMECO; verify directly with SMECO before assuming parity.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 net metering caps/sizing. Choptank publishes its own supplemental interconnection capacity guidance: individual interconnections are restricted to no larger than 3 MVA on 12kV circuits and 5 MVA on 25kV circuits -- a circuit-voltage-class-based ceiling ABOVE the state's 2MW net-metering cap itself, relevant mainly to larger C&I/grid-supply projects seeking non-net-metered interconnection or exceeding net-metering-eligible size. Choptank markets aggregation, solar, net metering, AND energy storage together on a single program page, suggesting more explicit co-op-level support/guidance for storage-paired systems than some peers.
storage_specific_notes: Choptank's marketing groups 'Solar, Net Metering, Aggregation & Energy Storage' together -- suggests an established storage-interconnection pathway, but specific grid-charging/non-export terms not independently retrieved this pass (page required JavaScript, could not fetch full text).

rule_summary: Municipal utility; follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps/sizing but reports its own local net-metered solar capacity: 3.49 MW installed as of 6/30/2025 (per PSC Net Metering Report). No charge to install a net meter at Easton (a favorable deviation vs. utilities that pass through meter costs). Easton allows aggregate NEM combining a single host account with child accounts under the statewide aggregation rules for agricultural/municipal/nonprofit entities.

Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps. Delmarva's PSC storage pilot is notably different in character from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's substation-scale utility-owned BESS: Delmarva contracted with Sunverge Energy to deploy BEHIND-THE-METER residential battery systems in 110 homes in Elk Neck, networked together to function as a virtual power plant (aggregated 0.5 MW / 1.5 MWh). This IS the closest match in the MD pilot program to a customer-sited/BYOD-style storage model referenced in the research brief -- distinguish from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's utility-owned substation/grid-asset pilots, which are NOT customer-owned-device programs.
storage_specific_notes: Elk Neck VPP (Sunverge, 110 homes, 0.5MW/1.5MWh aggregated) is the pilot most resembling a BYOD/customer-storage model in MD; confirm current operational status and whether it has a successor commercial program before assuming it's still active as of 2026.

utility_name: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
rule_summary: Dominion's residential/small-C&I tariff sub-caps nonresidential systems at 1 MW (below the 3 MW statewide statutory ceiling). Following the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order (Case No. PUR-2025-00079), Dominion is rolling out a 'NEM 2.0' tariff for customers who interconnect after the order's effective date: 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting are preserved, but the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate rises to $0.05829/kWh (includes a new $0.01/kWh credit for avoided RPS/REC compliance cost) and a $1/month administrative fee applies. The SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 application fee and its proposed 30-minute netting/dollar-based interval crediting. Pre-order NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered indefinitely and may switch to NEM 2.0 only if it becomes more favorable to them. Low-income customers may choose whichever tariff (legacy or NEM 2.0) is more favorable. Separately, the SCC-authorized standby charge threshold rises from 15 kW AC to 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 under HB 1255.
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of prior-year peak load statewide; Dominion-specific current subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: Legacy (NEM 1.0): year-end excess at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, last published 2019 figure); NEM 2.0 (new interconnections after ~mid-2026): $0.05829/kWh year-end excess cash-out, effective per April 30, 2026 SCC order
ic_application_fee: $0 application fee (SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 fee); $1/month administrative fee applies to NEM 2.0 customers only
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not published as a distinct kW threshold beyond standard Level 1/2/3 SGF review tiers
external_disconnect: Required per Dominion Terms and Conditions Section XXV for net-metered generating facilities
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited (grid-charged battery discharge is not distinguished from PV export in metering; Off-Peak Plan customers have export credited at the on/off/super-off-peak rate of the interval generated)
standby_charge: $2.79/kW distribution + $1.40/kW transmission standby charge per month on Schedules 1/1G (approx.); $4.19/kW distribution + $1.32/kW transmission on Schedule 1S; charge is based on the customer's peak monthly kW pulled from the grid, not on generation
standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 (raised from 15 kW AC under HB 1255; was 10 kW AC 2011-earlier revision)
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system does not by itself void grandfathering under the April 2026 SCC order language ('nothing...shall affect any eligible customer-generator...who interconnect before the effective date'), but any change in interconnected AC nameplate capacity requires a new interconnection application per company practice, and if the resulting aggregate AC capacity crosses the 15/20 kW standby-charge threshold it will newly trigger the standby charge — this specific battery-retrofit scenario is not explicitly addressed in Dominion's public net metering materials and should be confirmed directly with the company (flagged in gaps file). AC-coupled vs DC-coupled battery treatment and metering configuration requirements are not detailed in sources reviewed.

rule_summary: SCC Final Order (Aug. 29, 2025) largely rejected APCo's proposed net metering overhaul. APCo had sought to cut net-excess-generation compensation by ~70% (from ~8c/kWh to as low as 4.7c/kWh) and to add new grid-connection/standby charges; the SCC rejected the standby charge entirely and rejected switching from 12-month to hourly netting. Full retail 1:1 credit for self-consumed solar within the 12-month banking period is preserved. Net excess generation (true excess beyond annual consumption) is now compensated at a rate that includes REC value and exceeds the prior default PJM LMP-based avoided-cost rate. The 6% aggregate cap was retained (APCo had sought a reduction).
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of prior-year peak load (state default; APCo-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed)
export_credit_value: Net excess generation (annual true-up) compensated at avoided-cost/PJM LMP-based rate plus REC value, now higher than the prior straight avoided-cost figure (~3.5c/kWh, 2019); full retail 1:1 credit preserved for self-consumed generation
standby_charge: None — the SCC's August 29, 2025 order explicitly rejected APCo's proposed standby/grid-connection charge; monthly Basic (customer) charge remains $7.96/month, unchanged by the order
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge in APCo Virginia territory as of the 2025 order)
storage_specific_notes: Not directly addressed in sources reviewed for the battery-retrofit/grandfathering question; APCo's standard Net Metering Terms and Conditions state system sizing must not exceed annual usage to retain rollover eligibility, so a battery addition that increases interconnected AC capacity could still trigger a new interconnection review even though no standby charge exists in APCo territory.

rule_summary: Following the PSC's August 2025 base rate case order, AEP-WV ended 1:1 retail net metering for new customers. Customers whose net metering interconnection APPLICATION was submitted on or before February 28, 2026 are grandfathered onto full 1:1 retail crediting. Customers who apply after that date are subject to a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate, roughly a 27% cut from the effective 1:1 value) instead of 1:1 crediting. The PSC granted APCo/Wheeling Power customers a full extra year of grandfathering runway beyond what the company originally requested.
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of aggregate WV peak demand (state default; 0.5% reserved for residential); AEP-WV-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: ~12.4 cents/kWh fixed export credit for new (post-grandfathering-deadline) customers; 1:1 full retail for customers who applied by 2/28/2026
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 required for systems not meeting Level 1 criteria (effectively >25 kW or non-UL-1741-SB-certified equipment)
external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter per AEP TIIR
standby_charge: None identified — the 2025 PSC order restructured the export credit rate rather than adding a distinct standby/demand charge
storage_specific_notes: Not directly addressed in sources reviewed; because grandfathering is keyed to interconnection APPLICATION DATE rather than a system-composition test, adding a battery to an already-grandfathered (pre-2/28/2026) system likely does not by itself forfeit 1:1 status, but this is not explicitly confirmed by AEP-WV public materials and should be verified directly (flagged in gaps file).

Wheeling Power's WV service territory is limited to the Wheeling/Ohio County area.

rule_summary: Per the Feb. 16, 2024 PSC-approved settlement (effective March 27, 2024) resolving the companies' net-energy-metering base-rate case: customers who were net metering customers BEFORE the settlement's cutover are grandfathered onto full 1:1 retail bill offset for 25 years. New NEM customers interconnecting ON OR AFTER January 1, 2025 receive fixed credit rates instead of 1:1: 9.34 cents/kWh (residential, schools, churches, general service), 9.15 cents/kWh (large general service), 8.91 cents/kWh (large power/alternative generation). These new-customer rates are fixed for 2025-2026 and subject to renegotiation in the companies' 2026 ENEC (Expanded Net Energy Cost) case. Excess is credited only against the energy portion of the bill, not fixed/demand charges.

rule_summary: REC operates net metering under its Net Energy Metering Rider (2023) pursuant to Va. Code § 56-594.01 (co-op-specific statute). Individual system cap: 20 kW AC residential, 1,000 kW AC nonresidential; system may not be sized to produce more than 100% of the customer's trailing 12-month usage. 1:1 kWh credit with indefinite monthly rollover of banked credits. After 12 months on the program, customers may optionally elect a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) that buys out banked excess kWh at REC's avoided wholesale cost (roughly 30-40% of retail rate), zeroing the bank. REC also offers a separate Community Solar Rider (SSR) sold in 50 kWh blocks, available to any residential member regardless of net metering status. REC's TOU rate (Schedule A-1-TOU) is explicitly NOT available to net metering customers.

utility_name: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (Con Edison)
rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR for process and timelines, but its territory is dominated by underground secondary-network and spot-network grid, which changes what interconnection actually costs. Con Edison publishes CESIR cost ranges of up to about $20,000 for inverter-based systems and about $27,000 for rotating machines. On spot/isolated networks the default is a reverse-power relay that prevents export; since 2012 Con Edison offers Communications Aided Tripping (CAT) - insensitive network-protector settings plus SCADA, anti-islanding and DNP3 telemetry - to allow export on network service, at a project cost on the order of $100,000. Con Edison states it is the only utility in the nation allowing export on network service. Interconnection portal split at 50 kW-AC (Small DG vs Large DG); for hybrid projects the portal is chosen by export capability rather than combined nameplate. 2026 Customer Benefit Contribution: net-metered PV $1.29/kW-mo residential and $1.47/kW-mo small commercial; Value Stack PV $0.65 and $1.03.
ic_study_trigger_kw: In underground secondary network areas a CESIR may be required even for systems at or below 50 kW (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1); Con Edison-published CESIR cost up to ~$20,000 inverter-based and ~$27,000 rotating machine.
non_export_option: Yes - reverse power relay preventing export is Con Edison's traditional approach on spot and isolated networks; CAT is the paid alternative that permits export.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes - see state row. Con Edison requires charging kW (peak kW/kVA needed to charge) to be stated in the application scope of work; if it exceeds the local service, service upgrades may be required.
standby_charge: Standby Service under General Rule 20, plus the Rider Q Standby Pilot Rate Program (customer-selected contract demand and As-Used demand period) and SC-11 Buy-Back Service (LBMP, grossed up by 1.066 for secondary-level deliveries). Published standby rates (as of retrieval): residential contract demand $6.05/kW plus $20 customer charge; small business $8.77/kW plus $33; large commercial low-tension under 1,500 kW $9.18/kW plus $71.
standby_threshold_kw: 50 - customers with Contract Demand below 50 kW are reported exempt from mandatory Standby Service billing under General Rule 20.3, as are customers whose on-site generation nameplate is no more than 15% of maximum potential demand served from all sources. This aligns the standby threshold with the SIR's 50 kW expedited/large-project boundary. Threshold is SECONDARY-sourced - not read in the General Rule 20 tariff leaf.
storage_specific_notes: Con Edison states that SC1 residential customers under 25 kW-AC and SC2 small commercial customers under 2 MW-AC who install an ESS after 2017-03-10 receive Phase One NEM compensation, and that residential and small commercial customers are eligible to pair grid-parallel storage with solar and take service under Phase One NEM - i.e. adding a battery does not by itself force a move off Phase One NEM. Storage may only be added to a Phase One NEM system if it is paired with another Phase One NEM-eligible technology. Adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed as a Battery Energy Storage application with SIR Appendix K; a new PV plus new storage project is filed as a single Hybrid application. Metering: three acceptable hybrid configurations - exclusive ESS charge from PV, PV export only, and separate metering; the PSC approved a three-meter configuration for hybrid ESS in Case 18-E-0081, Order Modifying Standardized Interconnection Requirements issued 2018-04-19. Technologies behind one meter that are credited under different rate structures require specialized metering and/or relaying. NOTE: this guide is Version 4, July 2022, aligned to the May 2022 SIR - re-verify against the 2026-02-09 SIR.

utility_name: Long Island Power Authority / PSEG Long Island
rule_summary: Does NOT follow the New York State SIR. LIPA is a state authority outside PSC jurisdiction and PSL 66-j/66-l do not apply to it. Interconnection runs under LIPA's own Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGIP), an addendum to LIPA's Tariff for Electric Service, administered by PSEG Long Island as LIPA's agent, with a separate Smart Grid SGIP (SGSGIP) track. Scope is broader than the state SIR: distributed generation facilities with a nameplate rating of 10 MW or less aggregated on the customer side of the point of common coupling, versus 5 MW under the PSC SIR. Applications go through PSEG Long Island's Interconnection Online Application Portal (live since 2021-02-12). Separate PSEG Long Island technical requirements documents cover DER up to 500 kVA and above 500 kVA.
ic_application_fee: SGIP application fee $750 for 50 kW to 5 MW and $750 for 5 MW to 10 MW, payable to PSEG Long Island (SGIP Application Instructions, https://www.psegliny.com/aboutpseglongisland/ratesandtariffs/sgip/applications). Fee for systems under 50 kW not verified.
